description: A lockless transposition table lets several threads probe and store entries without locks. Each entry is packed into one 64-bit word, and the slot holds that word next to a second word, the word XOR-ed with the position's key; a probe reads both and takes the entry only if XOR-ing them gives the key back. If another thread wrote the slot in between, the check fails and the probe misses instead of returning a torn entry. The packing has limits: move and score must fit 48 bits together, entries deeper than 62 plies are not stored, and the slot checks 64 bits of the key. Here it is `PackedTable`, behind the `parallel` feature; use it for Lazy SMP when moves and scores are small, and the locked `SharedTable` otherwise.

papers.title: A lockless transposition-table implementation for parallel search

lineage.source: game-tree-search, src/table/packed.rs: "A transposition table several threads search with at once, without locks: each entry is packed into one 64-bit word, stored next to that word XOR-ed with the key (Hyatt and Mann's lockless hashing)."
